clue.text: Enter lift, disorderly charge to get in first

indicators.note: the clue says the word in is to get in first, so it heads the assembly
disorderly says the letters of lift are put out of order

parts.note: a charge is a rate, as in a fee

explanation.surface: Someone told to step into a lift and barge ahead of everyone in a disorderly scramble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enter' looks like an instruction but is the definition. 'disorderly' shuffles LIFT into FILT, and 'to get in first' puts IN at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To infiltrate a place is to get into it, typically covertly, so it is a synonym of enter.

clue.text: Pine fixture in kitchen

indicators.note: a fixture in a room is fixed inside it, so the letters sit within the word

explanation.surface: A pine unit fitted in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like wood for the kitchen fitting but is the verb: to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to long or yearn for it.

clue.text: Divine class of 14-year-olds in report?

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the class name is heard rather than written

parts.note: in British schools, a class like 4C of the fourth form holds pupils of about fourteen

explanation.surface: A religious studies class of teenagers mentioned in a school report.
explanation.walkthrough: British school classes are named by year and letter, like 4C; the fourth form is around age fourteen.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine the future is to predict it, the verb sense of divine.

clue.text: One's dying to make this pay!

definitions.text: One's dying to make this pay!

parts.words: One's dying to make this pay!
parts.note: dying to normally means eager, but here one must literally die for the policy to pay out

explanation.surface: Someone desperately keen to make an investment profitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy paying a sum on the holder's death only pays when someone actually dies.

clue.text: Creative arts, none booming

indicators.note: creative means inventive, so the letters of arts and none are made into something new

explanation.surface: Creative arts are not booming at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, echoing voice or sound is booming, or resonant.

clue.text: Twisted ungodly act — occasionally it could be gripping

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the picked letters are read backwards
occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A wicked deed, twisted, might be thrilling at times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters, NOLAT, which 'Twisted' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's claw grips its prey, a literal sense of gripping.

clue.text: Garment from southern India a queen wears

indicators.note: wears means the outer letters have the others on, i.e. around them

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A garment from the south of India that a queen puts on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a queen wears' says A and R go inside S and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a draped dress, a garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Classic that will be read in language lesson

indicators.note: the run of letters can be read inside the phrase, across the two words

explanation.surface: A classic text to be read in a language class.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic work is timeless, never going out of date.

clue.text: Popular hospital dept's broken toy with no zip?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: the hospital department has broken into the toy, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a dolly is a toy doll
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A child's popular toy broken in a hospital department, its zip gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a fastener but means energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lazily is doing it without energy or vigour, slang zip.

clue.text: Artist seen where arty types drink — from these?

indicators.note: an artist seen in a place is inside it, so the artist's letters sit within the venue

parts.note: arty types drink coffee in cafes
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist spotted in the bohemian cafes where creative people drink, perhaps drinking from these.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: what the arty types drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: Carafes are glass jugs from which wine or water is poured and drunk.

clue.text: See what I'm trying to say?

definitions.text: See what I'm trying to say?

parts.words: See what I'm trying to say?
parts.note: taken literally, this is seeing speech rather than hearing it, which a deaf person does by watching mouths

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker asking whether the listener understands the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To read speech from mouth movements is literally to see what someone says.

clue.text: Maybe steam sauce that's designed to impress

parts.note: steam is an example of power
a dressing is a sauce for a salad

explanation.surface: A steamed sauce prepared to wow guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for clothing chosen to impress, so 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing formal, authoritative clothes at work to project confidence is a fashion style aimed at impact.

clue.text: Cricketer's skill with revolver — it should make a good yarn

definitions.text: it should make a good yarn

parts.note: spinning the ball is a bowler's skill in cricket
a wheel is something that revolves

explanation.surface: A cricketer who is also handy with a gun should have a good story to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' suggests a gun and 'yarn' a story; both are taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This device twists fibre into thread, so a good one makes good yarn.

clue.text: Enjoy welcoming knight who French let go

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the word for enjoy holds the others

parts.note: to relish is to enjoy
N is the chess notation for a knight
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: Enjoying the company of a knight whom the French released.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or release something, such as a claim or power, is a synonym phrase for this verb.

clue.text: Fifty-fifty odds on getting good service

parts.note: evens is the betting price for a fifty-fifty chance

explanation.surface: A gambler with an even-money bet hoping for good service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the evening prayer service of the Anglican church.

clue.text: Cooler to be employed in backing Ono, Sir Paul

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
letters employed in a phrase are used within it, so the run is hidden there

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cool job going with Yoko Ono and Sir Paul McCartney, backing them as musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'to be employed'; those words are the hidden-word signal ('employed in'), so the definition is 'Cooler' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is slang for a jail, the place where convicts are locked up.

clue.text: Uplifting pop records? Absolute babble

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: LPs are long-playing pop records
utter means absolute, as in utter nonsense

explanation.surface: Cheery pop records that are nothing but complete nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Spluttering speech is incoherent and confused, much like babble.

clue.text: This person's left something from China, say

parts.note: the setter's this person is I, and with 's (is, read as am) that gives I'm
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone has left behind a piece of china, perhaps a vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like crockery but is the country; goods from abroad are imports.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods brought in from abroad, such as Chinese products, are imports.

clue.text: Speed to surround referee — one gets in the book first

definitions.text: one gets in the book first

indicators.note: the word for speed goes round the referee's letters

parts.note: pace is speed

explanation.surface: A speedy player hemming in the referee, the first to be booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the book' suggests a football booking; it means in a book's opening pages.
explanation.definitionFit: An author's introduction comes before the main text of a book.

clue.text: Run over Victor — in shock or OK?

indicators.note: in places the run, over and Victor letters inside the word for shock

parts.note: to shock is to appal
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone runs over a man called Victor: is he shocked or fine?
explanation.definitionFit: Giving the OK to something is giving it approval or consent.

clue.text: Rocking on vocal, one issues hot stuff

indicators.note: rocking means shaking about, so the letters of on and vocal are jumbled

explanation.surface: A singer rocking on vocals, belting out hot numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain that erupts spews lava, which is hot material.

clue.text: Lawyer opposing pieces local officials broadcast

parts.note: in chess each side has a queen, so the opposing pieces are queens

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard, so it is spelt as its sound-alike

parts.note: a council is a body of local government officials

explanation.surface: A lawyer opposing some articles that local officials have put out.
explanation.walkthrough: A Queen's Counsel was a senior barrister in Britain (now King's Counsel).
explanation.definitionFit: A senior barrister appointed on the monarch's behalf is a kind of lawyer.

clue.text: S American native reserved and turned up

parts.note: coy means shy or reserved

indicators.note: turned means flipped over, so the letters of up are reversed

explanation.surface: A shy South American native who turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: This large rodent is native to South America, now also found wild elsewhere.

clue.text: They kill members

definitions.meaning: limbs are members of the body

explanation.surface: Killers who belong to a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both weapons and the upper limbs of the body.

clue.text: Pictures created by writer — one's a peculiar grey

parts.note: one is I, and 's (is, read as am) makes I'm

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters of grey are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author confessing to being an odd grey sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers build mental pictures with figurative language, known collectively by this word.

clue.text: Where planes may fly and luggage disappear?

definitions.text: Where planes may fly and luggage disappear?

parts.words: Where planes may fly and luggage disappear?
parts.note: aircraft fly high in the rarefied atmosphere, and lost things vanish into it, as the idiom has it

explanation.surface: A grumble about air travel, where planes fly and bags go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: High altitude has rarefied atmosphere, and things that vanish without trace go into it idiomatically.

clue.text: Wishes to offload power tools

indicators.note: to offload is to unload, so the power letter is removed

parts.note: hopes are wishes

explanation.surface: Someone longing to get rid of their power tools.
explanation.definitionFit: These are garden implements for weeding, so they are tools.

clue.text: Not in fashion, American clothes old and horrible

indicators.note: clothes means dresses, so the letters for not in, fashion and American wrap around old

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
the rage is the current fashion

explanation.surface: An unfashionable American wearing dreadful old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in fashion' reads as one idea but splits in two. 'clothes' has the first three pieces dress the O, which sits before the final pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shocking and dreadful can be called horrible, a near synonym.
